messages:
marta: Quick sanity check — brought up mariner-embed-mini (384d, 512 dim) on int4. Small holdout mini-bench shows a weird kink in recall@1 for short queries (<=5 tokens).

sachin: Can you paste the eval command + quick numbers?

marta: sure, run:
```
./eval/runner.py --model mariner-embed-mini --quant int4 --pooling mean --holdout-size 5000 --queries short,mid,long --metrics recall@1,recall@10,silhouette
```
Results (holdout=5k):
- short: R@1 0.58 (baseline 0.67), R@10 0.82 (0.86)
- mid:   R@1 0.66 (0.65), R@10 0.88 (0.87)
- long:  R@1 0.69 (0.70), R@10 0.90 (0.91)

ben: huh — drop only on short queries. clustering/purity numbers?

marta: silhouette drops for short queries from 0.21 -> 0.12. Top-1 label flip rate up 3.4% vs baseline.

sachin: could be pooling / tokenization. mariner uses a slightly different BOS handling. Try CLS pooling and re-run.

marta: re-ran with CLS pooling, int4:
- short: R@1 0.63 (baseline 0.67)
- mid:   0.65
- long:  0.69
silhouette short -> 0.18

ben: okay improvement. maybe int4 quantization interacts with mean pooling for short sequences (low token mass). Try per-channel vs symmetric quant schedule?

marta: opened a quick experiment: per-channel int4 + mean pooling queued on ci. ID 5219.

ci-bot: CI job 5219 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/mariner/5219/summary.json

sachin: can you throw example hard queries (short) and their nearest neighbors? a few negative examples would help debug.

marta: pasted a couple examples in the run artifacts; also added script to diff nearest neighbor tokens. i'll slot a short triage tomorrow.

ben: great. for next steps: 1) validate per-channel int4 on holdout sweep, 2) run iso-holdout (same corpus but longer contexts) to check prefix sensitivity, 3) add short-query-focused prompts to our regression alerts.

marta: ack. creating eval ticket and will update with the artifact link + reproducible scripts. :thumbsup:
